key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C self-fluxing coatings can be tuned from low-friction to high-wear-resistance behavior by adjusting barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay, but the best tribology depends on which performance target is prioritized.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical process window for restoring and hardening machine parts with coatings that balance density, hardness, roughness, and wear resistance.
method: Varied detonation-spraying conditions: barrel filling level (48–68%), O/C ratio (1.026–1.856), and inter-shot delay (0–1 s).
Characterized coating morphology, thickness, porosity/cracking, roughness, hardness, friction, and specific wear rate.
Compared trade-offs between dense low-porosity deposition and microcrack formation under higher loading conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evaluation of friction, wear rate, roughness, and hardness, including a minimum friction coefficient of 0.674 ± 0.136, a wear rate as low as 0.000189 mm³/(N·m), Ra reduction from 5.00 to 3.60 μm, and hardness up to 905.6 HV.
watch_item: Optimizing for lower friction can increase wear, so implementation should not rely on a single metric without matching the coating to the service environment.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
